column1: # Files that a stock install ships WITH capabilities, so getcap output can be triaged.
# caps must list exactly the capabilities the distro grants (comma separated, no flags) for
# the row to count as "expected". Anything else - extra caps, or a path that is not in here -
# is reported on its own merits from capabilities.tsv.

column5: description
iputils ping. Needs raw sockets; this replaced the old SUID bit and is the normal state on a modern distro.
iputils ping with raw-socket capability instead of SUID.
IPv6 ping; raw sockets only.
Sends ARP requests; raw sockets only.
iputils clockdiff; raw sockets only.
iputils tracepath; raw sockets only.
iputils traceroute6; raw sockets only.
mtr's privileged helper; raw sockets only.
fping; raw sockets only.
Wireshark's capture process. Expected if wireshark-cli is installed and you chose the "non-root capture" option; it does mean anyone in the wireshark group can sniff the network.
Wireshark's capture process; lets the wireshark group sniff traffic.
shadow's helper for rootless containers. cap_setuid looks alarming but it only writes uid_map for the calling namespace.
shadow's helper for rootless containers; writes gid_map only.
Locks secrets into memory that cannot be swapped to disk.
Ships this way on a few distros so it can read DMI tables. cap_dac_override is very strong for what it does - worth confirming against your package manager.
Present on some systemd builds; verify with your package manager.
Reserved-port binding for the r-services. Should not be installed at all on a modern host.
Reserved-port binding for the r-services. Should not be installed at all.
Reserved-port binding for the r-services. Should not be installed at all.
Apache's suexec with capabilities instead of SUID. Only expected on a web server.
